citation.description: RebarArgumentParser.__init__ sets self.color = False after super().__init__, disabling ANSI colorization on Python 3.14 (inert on 3.12). Two new tests in test_cli_parser_contract.py (test_help_and_usage_are_never_colorized, test_subparsers_inherit_the_uncolored_pin) force FORCE_COLOR=1 and assert no \x1b in output.

criteria.criterion: AC1: the test passes on both Python 3.12 and Python 3.14. Verified by running it under both interpreters.

citation.description: Test asserts both code == 2 and err.startswith('usage: rebar audit'), independently binding on exit code and usage line. render_parse_error in _parser.py writes usage to stderr and returns 2.

criteria.criterion: AC2: it still fails if the CLI stops emitting a usage line or stops exiting 2. Verified by mutation.

citation.description: The only other startswith assertions in the file use custom usage= strings (line 156) or subprocess stdout (line 271), not rendered argparse text. The root fix (color=False) covers all RebarArgumentParser instances globally. The ticket notes 25 failures across 9 modules were all fixed by the same one-line change.

criteria.criterion: AC3: sibling assertions in the file that match on rendered argparse text are audited and given the same treatment, or explicitly noted as safe.

citation.description: Commit e40139de3f75ed23380ec59d03f2c1ce365ee920 adds self.color = False to RebarArgumentParser.__init__, fixing the root cause. The test at test_advanced_cli_parsers.py:124 still asserts startswith('usage: rebar audit') which now works on both Python versions.

criteria.criterion: Bug 'CLI parser test breaks under Python 3.14 argparse color' is actually resolved: the reported defect no longer reproduces and expected behavior holds.
